intelligence.human_view: Every room in a house has the same walls and the same roof — only the middle changes: the kitchen has a stove, the bedroom has a bed, the mail room has the letters. That is the One-System Law: one frame, the Hub, and a function is a change of the center, nothing else. The Messenger rounds kept building new houses instead of furnishing the room — a cover here, pills there, a different family — and each drift had to be repaired by another round. The law ends the drift at the root: start from the Hub frame, and you cannot build a different family by accident. And the same eye test judges the work: if the page looks exactly the same in the first second, nothing changed — however many checks it passed.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine every room in your house has the same walls and the same roof — only the middle is different. The kitchen has a stove, the bedroom has a bed. That's one system. And if you tidy your room but it looks exactly the same when Dad walks in, you didn't really change anything — you have to change what he sees first, and show him a picture of before and after.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, it's like a house, love — the same walls, the same roof, dear, only the middle changes, dear. The kitchen has the stove, dear, the bedroom has the bed, dear. That's one system, dear. And if you tidy your room, dear, but it looks exactly the same when Dad walks in, dear, you haven't really changed anything, dear — you change what he sees first, dear, and you show him the before and after, dear.
